key_insight: A physics-assisted neural closure can better model compressible velocity-gradient dynamics by jointly learning thermodynamic-gradient contributions, especially the baroclinic and pressure-Hessian effects.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate surrogate for high-Mach CFD, helping predict small-scale turbulence behavior in compressible flows with vibrational non-equilibrium.
method: Builds a hybrid enhanced homogenized Euler equation (H-EHEE) model for velocity-gradient evolution.
Combines phenomenological closures for pressure-Hessian dynamics with a neural-network closure for inviscid baroclinic tensor generation.
Adds a data-driven closure for vibrational non-equilibrium and uses a novel tensor basis that can represent non-symmetric features.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated against direct numerical simulation across multiple turbulent Mach numbers and showed close agreement with DNS, with especially strong gains in highly compressible regimes.
watch_item: Because the framework mixes learned and phenomenological components, robustness outside the training Mach-number range and sensitivity to tensor-basis design should be checked carefully.
paper_title: A physics-assisted deep neural network-based closure framework for velocity gradient dynamics in compressible flows with vibrational non-equilibrium
